# Gladly API (1.0)

Download OpenAPI specification: Download

#  Introducing the Gladly API

At Gladly, we believe that customer service is best when it's a conversation.
That means more than just helping customers with one-off questions or issues: it's about making them feel known, valued, and respected for the individuals they are.

The Gladly API was built to help facilitate those relationships, providing agents with the rich customer context
they need to deliver seamless experiences that make customers feel like they're more than just a number in a sea of others.

#  Overview

You can integrate easily with Gladly by calling Gladly's REST API and implementing the Lookup API to provide data from your own services.

Some examples of what you do through Gladly APIs include managing customer profile data, interacting with a customer's timeline,
providing the latest information about a customer's orders, and more.

##  REST API

Clients can access the **REST API** via HTTPS at your organization's Gladly domain (e.g. `{organization}.gladly.com` ).

Resources follow REST semantics and utilize industry-standard HTTP verbs, response codes, and authentication schemes.
In addition, all responses and payloads are in JSON with consistent error codes and formats.

##  Lookup API

The Gladly **Lookup API** allows your organization to provide data services to power the agent's experience with a complete view of your customers'
information, transactions, and activity. You can provide a web service that implements the Lookup API and Gladly will call it when that data is needed.

Like the REST API, the Lookup API is specified using REST semantics, and exchanges JSON requests and responses authenticated and signed with secure keys.

...

#  Getting Started

Think of this section as getting the keys to unlocking your access to the Gladly APIs.
First, you'll need to set up an account with the necessary API permissions .
With these permissions, you can then go on to create the API Token(s) you need to access Gladly's API resources .

##  Permissions

Gladly Administrators can set API permissions on an agent-by-agent basis.
We'll discuss how this maps to API access in the section on authentication below.

To allow a user to create API tokens and access the API:

2. Open the menu on the top left-hand corner of the page.
3. Navigate to **Settings** > _\*Users_
4. Search and click the user profile you wish to give access to.
5. You'll see a permission called **API User** . Select it, while making sure to keep the user's **Agent** role intact.
6. Hit **Save** to give access.

Agent profile screen

We recommend creating a dedicated user to make API calls, whose account won't be used for agent and organization management.
This will help you with any future audits of API activity vs. agent activity.

##  Creating API Tokens

You must create an API token to access Gladly API resources (see above Permissions ).
If your profile already has access to the **API User** permission, you'll see a menu item titled **More settings** . Click **More settings** :

API Token Menu

Click **API Tokens** , then the **Create Token** button on the upper right-hand corner of the page:

API Token Add

A token will be generated and named, by default, **New Token** (though depending on whether you have existing tokens, it may be named New Token 2, or New Token 3, etc.).
You can rename the token to something more easily referenceable by clicking the name to edit.

This token will be associated with your agent profile, which we refer to as the API User in this document.

API Token View

For security purposes, you'll only see a new token once before you navigate away from the page.

##  Replacing/Rotating API Tokens

Should you lose this token, or wish to rotate your application keys, you can do the following:

1. Generate a new token.
2. Store the new token in a secure location.
3. Delete the old token.
4. Update your applications/scripts with the new token.

#  Authentication

##  BasicAuth

Gladly API uses token-based **Basic Authentication** . API tokens are associated with designated Gladly users.
To create and use an API token, your user must have the API User permission. An API token can be used to perform any API request without restriction.

|user name |password |
| --- | --- |
|agent email |API token |

The credentials must be passed via an `Authorization` HTTP header. All requests must be made over HTTPS.

```
curl  -u user@organization.com: $GLADLY_API_TOKEN \ 
organization.gladly.com/api/v1/organization
```

|Security Scheme Type |HTTP |
| --- | --- |
|HTTP Authorization Scheme |basic |

Simply choose where to send notifications about events that you are interested in (e.g. when a conversation is closed), and they’ll be delivered to the endpoint of your choice.

Configure webhooks using the Webhooks API or the Webhooks Admin Page.

Users with API User permissions can configure webhooks by navigating to Integrations > Webhooks.

Webhooks admin page

##  Securing Webhooks

We provide two methods for your web service to authenticate requests from Gladly.
We recommend implementing at least one **authentication** option.

### Basic Authentication

For this method you will supply a username and password with the webhooks `credentials` field. This will be sent with each request. You may optionally supply a realm if needed.

### Header Based Token Authentication

For this method you will configure one or more HTTP headers with the webhook's `headers` field. Gladly will send in each request to your web service.

results.title: Set up MCP connections - Gladly Help and Product Docs
excerpts:
Set up MCP connections

Connect Gladly AI to an external MCP server so it can call that server's tools during Customer conversations. This article covers adding and testing a connection, then using its tools in a Guide. To learn how MCP connections work, see What are MCP connections?
[!WARNING] MCP tools reach Gladly AI only after you add them to a Guide or Skill.
Replies that use MCP tool data pass the same reply guardrails as any other Gladly AI reply.

Before you begin

Have the following ready for the MCP server you want to connect:
* The server URL, for example api.example.com/mcp
* The type of authentication the server uses: none, bearer token, API key, or OAuth (authorization code or client credentials)
* The credentials for that authentication type

Access MCP settings

1. Go to Settings.
2. Under App Developer Tools, select MCP.
The MCP page lists your connections on the Active and Inactive tabs. For each connection, the table shows the connection name, the server, its success rate, and its status.
MCP page with no connections configured.
If you haven't added a connection yet, the page prompts you to add one.
![](cdn.us.document360.io/7047b671-c4f2-4df0-bb0a-b9b511fd2452/Images/Documentation/mcp add connect.png?sv=2026-02-06&spr=https&st=2026-11-16T22%3A05%3A47Z&se=2026-11-16T23%3A05%3A47Z&sr=b&sp=r&sig=cwKD7TjPI2CJHMX%2FXVxoCd6y2KpZtlAwdccLSLCP27Y%3D)

Add a connection to a new MCP server

1. On the MCP page, select Add Connection.
2. Select the Server dropdown, then select + New MCP server.
3. Enter the Server URL.
4. Enter a Server name that helps your team recognize the server, for example "Retalè Footwear".
5. Select an Authentication type:
* None
* Bearer Token
* API Key
* OAuth (Authorization Code)
* OAuth (Client Credentials)
6. Enter the credentials for the authentication type you selected. For OAuth (Authorization Code), a sign-in window opens so you can authorize the connection.
7. (Optional) Enter a Description, for example "Store information, order status lookups, and product catalog search".
8. Enter a Connection name, for example "retale-footwear".
9. Keep Active turned on if you want the connection available right away.
10. Select Save. ![](cdn.us.document360.io/7047b671-c4f2-4df0-bb0a-b9b511fd2452/Images/Documentation/mcp server connection.png?sv=2026-02-06&spr=https&st=2026-11-16T22%3A05%3A47Z&se=2026-11-16T23%3A05%3A47Z&sr=b&sp=r&sig=jBTIA7G07tGgNlzD7%2FmKu7X4LcuYdmmCj9UMaFKO%2FQA%3D)
When the connection is saved, the Connection Added page confirms that the connection is saved. Select Test Tools to try one of the server's tools right away, or select Done to return to the MCP page.

Add another connection to an existing server

If your org already has a server registered, you can create another connection to it, for example to use different credentials.
1. On the MCP page, select Add Connection.
2. Select the Server dropdown and choose a server under Your servers. You can search by name or URL.
3. Enter a Connection name.
4. Keep Active turned on if you want the connection available right away.
5. Select Save.

Test the MCP

You have two test options: Test Connection checks that Gladly can reach the server and find its tools, and Test Tool runs one tool so you can review its output.
![](cdn.us.document360.io/7047b671-c4f2-4df0-bb0a-b9b511fd2452/Images/Documentation/testing mcp.png?sv=2026-02-06&spr=https&st=2026-11-16T22%3A05%3A47Z&se=2026-11-16T23%3A05%3A47Z&sr=b&sp=r&sig=%2Fx27Yg33Hix1drF%2F%2FwoBXmDpAMSGgDyo1YgNU7umHuA%3D)
[!NOTE] What is a tool?
In MCP, a tool is a single action an external server lets Gladly AI run, such as looking up an order or searching a product catalog. Each tool has a name, a description, and the inputs it needs, and it returns a result that Gladly AI can use in its reply. One MCP server can offer many tools, and Gladly discovers them automatically when you add a connection.

results.title: What is the Gladly MCP for Claude?
excerpts:
What is the Gladly MCP for Claude?

The Gladly MCP for Claude connects Claude to your Gladly organization. Once connected, you can use plain English in Claude to investigate AI sessions, spot patterns, improve Guides and Workflows, and test your changes before customers see them. To connect Claude, see Set up the Gladly MCP for Claude.
[!CAUTION] Not the same as MCP connections
The Gladly MCP for Claude lets Claude work in your Gladly organization. MCP connections do the opposite: they let Gladly AI call tools on your own servers during Customer conversations. The two features are separate and don't depend on each other.

How the Gladly MCP for Claude works

The Gladly MCP for Claude has two parts that you add to Claude: a plugin and a connector. The plugin adds a setup command that helps you connect. The connector gives Claude secure access to your Gladly organization and the knowledge it needs to work with Gladly AI, including Gladly Agents, Guides, Workflows, Actions, Knowledge, and the Simulator.
When you ask a question or make a request, Claude plans the work, reads what it needs from Gladly, and saves changes using your Gladly permissions. For example, you can ask, "Why are returns sessions being handed off?" Claude opens the sessions, reviews each step, and explains what happened.
Claude showing a visual report of Gladly AI sessions.
Claude acts as you Claude signs in with your own Gladly account and has the same permissions you do. Changes that Claude saves appear in Gladly as if you made them yourself. They also appear in the Changelog under your name, tagged "(MCP)."

...

What you can do

Claude helps you through the whole improvement loop: investigate a problem, estimate its impact, plan a fix, make the change, test it, and share what changed. You don't need to be technical. Start with a problem, and Claude suggests the next step and Gladly best practices along the way.
* Investigate: Find out what went wrong in one session or across a group of sessions.
* Analyze: Spot patterns across sessions, including which Workflows and steps ran, handoff and resolution rates, and results from Signals.
* Improve: Test changes to a Guide or Workflow before they go live.
* Build: Set up new Guides and Workflows from a description or a document, such as a policy or SOP.
* Understand Actions: Ask what a custom Action does, see its recent runs, and update it safely.
* Test at scale: Create Simulator Scenarios in plain English.
See Use the Gladly MCP for Claude for example prompts.

Requirements

To connect Claude to Gladly, you need all of the following:
* Your organization is in the beta. Gladly has enabled MCP access for your organization.
* You have an eligible role. You're a Team Manager, Compliance Admin, or Admin in Gladly, or you have a custom role with the Manage Gladly AI, View Gladly AI, or Review Gladly AI permission. Other roles can't connect.
* You use a supported version of Claude. You use Claude Desktop or claude.ai on a paid plan.
MCP is on for your whole organization MCP access is turned on for your organization as a whole, not person by person. You can't allow or block one specific person. Claude gets the same access as the person who connects, so only give eligible roles to people you trust with customer data and your AI setup.

Webhooks

Subscribe to 35+ event types including agent status changes, conversation lifecycle, customer profile updates, task events, and payment requests.

Rate Limits

* Default: 10 requests/second per method (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE)

results.title: What are MCP connections? - Gladly Help and Product Docs
excerpts:
What are MCP connections?

An MCP connection links Gladly AI to an external system so it can look up information or take action during a Customer Conversation. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets AI systems discover and call the tools an external system offers. With an MCP connection, Gladly AI can check an order status, search a product catalog, or look up store hours while it helps a customer, using live data from your own systems.
![](cdn.us.document360.io/7047b671-c4f2-4df0-bb0a-b9b511fd2452/Images/Documentation/mcp exchange.png?sv=2026-02-06&spr=https&st=2026-11-20T23%3A24%3A20Z&se=2026-11-21T00%3A24%3A20Z&sr=b&sp=r&sig=4it%2FtWTffbBsVff0vPNrOPeyyOOC9KO3%2BMlC30jGqvM%3D)
Instead of building a custom App Platform integration for every external system, you register an MCP server once. Gladly discovers the tools on that server automatically.

How MCP connections work

When a customer asks a question, Gladly AI decides whether one of your MCP tools can help. If it can, Gladly AI calls the tool on your MCP server, reads the response, and uses it to answer the customer.
For example, a customer asks, "Where is my order RT-1001?" Gladly AI calls an order lookup tool on your server, gets back the status, carrier, and tracking number, and shares them in its reply.
![](cdn.us.document360.io/7047b671-c4f2-4df0-bb0a-b9b511fd2452/Images/Documentation/connect gladly ai to mcp.png?sv=2026-02-06&spr=https&st=2026-11-20T23%3A24%3A20Z&se=2026-11-21T00%3A24%3A20Z&sr=b&sp=r&sig=MzqS2rMvnGM7nJjbscP0SorxeSzOHiI%2BiTlbI2ZmJR8%3D)

Servers, connections, and tools

Three terms describe how MCP fits together in Gladly:
* Server: The external system that offers tools, identified by its URL. For example, an MCP server for your order management system.
* Connection: How your org connects to a server. A connection has a name, the authentication details for the server, and an active or inactive status. You can create more than one connection to the same server, for example to use different credentials.
* Tool: A single capability the server offers, such as lookup_order_status or search_products. Each tool has a description and the inputs it needs.

Where Gladly AI uses MCP tools

MCP tools reach Gladly AI only after you add them to a Guide or Skill. Adding a connection on its own doesn't change how Gladly AI responds.
In a Guide, you wrap an MCP tool in a Custom Action, then add that Action to a Guide section. The Custom Action calls the MCP tool as one of its steps, and you control what the Action collects from the customer and what it passes to the tool. MCP tools work alongside your other Actions, so a single Guide can use both.
See Set up MCP connections for the steps.

Authentication options

Gladly supports the following authentication types for an MCP server:
* None
* Bearer Token
* API Key
* OAuth (Authorization Code)
* OAuth (Client Credentials)
Use the type your server requires. If you're not sure which one to use, ask the team that manages the server.

Manage MCP connections

You manage connections from Settings, under App Developer Tools, on the MCP page. From there you can:
* Add a connection to a new or existing server.

sources.title: What are MCP connections?
sources.trimmed:
An **MCP connection** links Gladly AI to an external system so it can look up information or take action during a Customer Conversation. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets AI systems discover and call the tools an external system offers. With an MCP connection, Gladly AI can check an order status, search a product catalog, or look up store hours while it helps a customer, using live data from your own systems.

Instead of building a custom App Platform integration for every external system, you register an MCP server once. Gladly discovers the tools on that server automatically.

---

## How MCP connections work

When a customer asks a question, Gladly AI decides whether one of your MCP tools can help. If it can, Gladly AI calls the tool on your MCP server, reads the response, and uses it to answer the customer.

For example, a customer asks, "Where is my order RT-1001?" Gladly AI calls an order lookup tool on your server, gets back the status, carrier, and tracking number, and shares them in its reply.

### Servers, connections, and tools

Three terms describe how MCP fits together in Gladly:

* **Server:** The external system that offers tools, identified by its URL. For example, an MCP server for your order management system.
* **Connection:** How your org connects to a server. A connection has a name, the authentication details for the server, and an active or inactive status. You can create more than one connection to the same server, for example to use different credentials.
* **Tool:** A single capability the server offers, such as `lookup_order_status` or `search_products`. Each tool has a description and the inputs it needs.

## Where Gladly AI uses MCP tools

MCP tools reach Gladly AI only after you add them to a Guide or Skill. Adding a connection on its own doesn't change how Gladly AI responds.

In a Guide, you wrap an MCP tool in a Custom Action, then add that Action to a Guide section. The Custom Action calls the MCP tool as one of its steps, and you control what the Action collects from the customer and what it passes to the tool. MCP tools work alongside your other Actions, so a single Guide can use both.

See Set up MCP connections for the steps.

## Authentication options

Gladly supports the following authentication types for an MCP server:

* **None**
* **Bearer Token**
* **API Key**
* **OAuth (Authorization Code)**
* **OAuth (Client Credentials)**

Use the type your server requires. If you're not sure which one to use, ask the team that manages the server.

## Manage MCP connections

You manage connections from **Settings**, under **App Developer Tools**, on the **MCP** page. From there you can:

* Add a connection to a new or existing server.
* Test a connection to confirm Gladly can reach the server and find its tools.
* Run a tool on its own to see what it returns.
* View tool call logs to see each request and response.
* Edit, deactivate, or delete a connection.

See Set up MCP connections for step-by-step instructions.

---

> Things to know
>
> * **Guardrails still apply.** Replies that use MCP tool data pass the same reply guardrails as any other Gladly AI reply. Gladly doesn't screen the tool's output itself, so make sure your server returns only information you're comfortable sharing with customers.
> * **Tools only.** MCP connections support tools. Resources and prompts offered by an MCP server aren't available.
> * **If a server is unreachable.** Gladly drops only that server's tools for that turn, and the rest of the conversation continues.
> * **Everything is logged.** Each tool call, including test runs, appears in the connection's tool call logs. Tool calls also appear in conversation history and action logs.

*Customer* or C*ustomers* refers to the people you support through Gladly who buy or use your products or services.

sources.title: Set up MCP connections
sources.trimmed:
Connect Gladly AI to an external MCP server so it can call that server's tools during Customer conversations. This article covers adding and testing a connection, then using its tools in a Guide. To learn how MCP connections work, see What are MCP connections?

> MCP tools reach Gladly AI only after you add them to a Guide or Skill.
>
> Replies that use MCP tool data pass the same reply guardrails as any other Gladly AI reply.

## Before you begin

Have the following ready for the MCP server you want to connect:

* The server URL, for example `https://api.example.com/mcp`
* The type of authentication the server uses: none, bearer token, API key, or OAuth (authorization code or client credentials)
* The credentials for that authentication type

## Access MCP settings

1. Go to **Settings**.
2. Under **App Developer Tools**, select **MCP**.

The **MCP** page lists your connections on the **Active** and **Inactive** tabs. For each connection, the table shows the connection name, the server, its success rate, and its status.

MCP page with no connections configured.

If you haven't added a connection yet, the page prompts you to add one.

## Add a connection to a new MCP server

1. On the **MCP** page, select **Add Connection**.
2. Select the **Server** dropdown, then select **+ New MCP server**.
3. Enter the **Server URL**.
4. Enter a **Server name** that helps your team recognize the server, for example "Retalè Footwear".
5. Select an **Authentication** type:

   * **None**
   * **Bearer Token**
   * **API Key**
   * **OAuth (Authorization Code)**
   * **OAuth (Client Credentials)**
6. Enter the credentials for the authentication type you selected. For OAuth (Authorization Code), a sign-in window opens so you can authorize the connection.
7. (Optional) Enter a **Description**, for example "Store information, order status lookups, and product catalog search".
8. Enter a **Connection name**, for example "retale-footwear".
9. Keep **Active** turned on if you want the connection available right away.
10. Select **Save**.

When the connection is saved, the **Connection Added** page confirms that the connection is saved. Select **Test Tools** to try one of the server's tools right away, or select **Done** to return to the **MCP** page.

### Add another connection to an existing server

If your org already has a server registered, you can create another connection to it, for example to use different credentials.

1. On the **MCP** page, select **Add Connection**.
2. Select the **Server** dropdown and choose a server under **Your servers**. You can search by name or URL.
3. Enter a **Connection name**.
4. Keep **Active** turned on if you want the connection available right away.
5. Select **Save**.

## Test the MCP

You have two test options: **Test Connection** checks that Gladly can reach the server and find its tools, and **Test Tool** runs one tool so you can review its output.

> What is a tool?
>
> In MCP, a tool is a single action an external server lets Gladly AI run, such as looking up an order or searching a product catalog. Each tool has a name, a description, and the inputs it needs, and it returns a result that Gladly AI can use in its reply. One MCP server can offer many tools, and Gladly discovers them automatically when you add a connection.
>
> Examples from a footwear store’s server:
>
> * `lookup_order_status`: takes an order number and returns the order’s status and tracking details.
> * `search_products`: takes a search phrase, such as “loafers”, and returns matching products with prices and sizes.
> * `get_store_hours`: takes no inputs and returns the store’s hours.

### Test a connection

Test a connection to confirm that Gladly can reach the server and discover its tools.

1. On the **MCP** page, select the menu at the end of the connection's row.
2. Select **Test Connection**.

A confirmation banner appears with the number of tools Gladly found on the server, for example "Connected - 3 tools available".

sources.title: What is the Gladly MCP for Claude?
sources.trimmed:
The Gladly MCP for Claude connects Claude to your Gladly organization. Once connected, you can use plain English in Claude to investigate AI sessions, spot patterns, improve Guides and Workflows, and test your changes before customers see them. To connect Claude, see Set up the Gladly MCP for Claude.

> Not the same as MCP connections
>
> The Gladly MCP for Claude lets Claude work in your Gladly organization. MCP connections do the opposite: they let Gladly AI call tools on your own servers during Customer conversations. The two features are separate and don't depend on each other.

## How the Gladly MCP for Claude works

The Gladly MCP for Claude has two parts that you add to Claude: a plugin and a connector. The plugin adds a setup command that helps you connect. The connector gives Claude secure access to your Gladly organization and the knowledge it needs to work with Gladly AI, including Gladly Agents, Guides, Workflows, Actions, Knowledge, and the Simulator.

When you ask a question or make a request, Claude plans the work, reads what it needs from Gladly, and saves changes using your Gladly permissions. For example, you can ask, "Why are returns sessions being handed off?" Claude opens the sessions, reviews each step, and explains what happened.

Claude showing a visual report of Gladly AI sessions.

**Claude acts as you** Claude signs in with your own Gladly account and has the same permissions you do. Changes that Claude saves appear in Gladly as if you made them yourself. They also appear in the Changelog under your name, tagged "(MCP)."

## What you can do

Claude helps you through the whole improvement loop: investigate a problem, estimate its impact, plan a fix, make the change, test it, and share what changed. You don't need to be technical. Start with a problem, and Claude suggests the next step and Gladly best practices along the way.

* **Investigate:** Find out what went wrong in one session or across a group of sessions.
* **Analyze:** Spot patterns across sessions, including which Workflows and steps ran, handoff and resolution rates, and results from Signals.
* **Improve:** Test changes to a Guide or Workflow before they go live.
* **Build:** Set up new Guides and Workflows from a description or a document, such as a policy or SOP.
* **Understand Actions:** Ask what a custom Action does, see its recent runs, and update it safely.
* **Test at scale:** Create Simulator Scenarios in plain English.

See Use the Gladly MCP for Claude for example prompts.

## Requirements

To connect Claude to Gladly, you need all of the following:

* **Your organization is in the beta.** Gladly has enabled MCP access for your organization.
* **You have an eligible role.** You're a Team Manager, Compliance Admin, or Admin in Gladly, or you have a custom role with the Manage Gladly AI, View Gladly AI, or Review Gladly AI permission. Other roles can't connect.
* **You use a supported version of Claude.** You use Claude Desktop or claude.ai on a paid plan.

**MCP is on for your whole organization** MCP access is turned on for your organization as a whole, not person by person. You can't allow or block one specific person. Claude gets the same access as the person who connects, so only give eligible roles to people you trust with customer data and your AI setup. For details, see Review security and data for the Gladly MCP for Claude.

> **Beta access is all or nothing**
>
